title: Paid and unpaid work

match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-types-work, covers paid versus unpaid work but is broader: it also teaches full-time, part-time and casual work, and its questions test those types rather than the value of unpaid work to the community, so no bank point matches this point exactly.

draft.title: Paid and unpaid work
card: Work done in return for income, such as a wage or salary. A nurse, a bus driver and a shop assistant all do paid work.
Work done without payment. Examples are caring for family, housework and volunteering.
Unpaid work still has value. A parent caring for a child, or a volunteer who coaches a junior sports team, provides help the community needs.
The same task can be paid or unpaid. Cooking dinner at home is unpaid work, but cooking it in a restaurant is paid work.
draft.remember: Work is paid or unpaid. Unpaid work still adds to the community.

a.q: Which of these is an example of unpaid work?
opts: Cleaning the house you live in with your family
Cleaning offices at night for a cleaning company
Cleaning a school hall for a weekly wage
Cleaning a hotel room as a casual employee
a.why: Housework for your own family is done without payment, so it is unpaid work. The other three are done in return for income, so they are paid work, even though the task is cleaning in each case.
a.clue: Look for the one where nobody pays the worker.

b.q: Priya spends Saturday mornings helping at a food bank in Geelong, and she is not paid. A student says her work is not really work because she earns no income. Which reply is best?
opts: It is unpaid work, and it still helps the community
It is not work, because only paid tasks count as work
It is paid work, because the food bank gains from it
It is only work if the food bank gives her a wage later
b.why: Volunteering is unpaid work. Work does not need to bring in income to be work, and the food bank's clients still gain from it. The tempting wrong option says only paid tasks count, but the card shows unpaid work is still work.
b.clue: Does a task stop being work when no one pays for it?

a.best: Cleaning the house you live in with your family

b.best: It is unpaid work, and it still helps the community
